# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tham_2017_insulin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tham_2017_insulin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.899> (open access, PMC5573917)

Tham 2017 fitted one population PK model (NONMEM 7.3, FOCE-I) to pooled
single-dose PK / euglycemic clamp data for six subcutaneous insulin products
and three premixes, then used the typical-value model in an R Shiny tool to
illustrate insulin regimens. The model has three disposition systems that do
not interact:

| System | Formulations (depots) | Shared parameters |
|---|---|---|
| Insulin glargine | `depot_glar` (first-order) + zero-order input into `central_glar` | CL/F, V/F (linear weight effect), F (dose effect) |
| Human insulin | regular U-100 `depot_regu100`, regular U-500 `depot_regu500`, NPH `depot_nph` (lagged) | CL/F (dose effect), V/F (power weight effect) |
| Insulin lispro | lispro `depot_lis` (lagged first-order) + zero-order input into `central_lis`; ILPS `depot_ilps` | CL/F, V/F (power weight effect) |

Premixes are dosed by component (Tham 2017 Methods): Mix 70/30 = 30% regular
U-100 + 70% NPH, Mix 50/50 = 50% lispro + 50% ILPS, Mix 75/25 = 25% lispro +
75% ILPS.

# Population

The model was developed from 16 clinical pharmacology studies in healthy
adults without diabetes (Tham 2017 Table 1): regular U-100 (N = 30), regular
U-500 (12), NPH (24), Mix 70/30 (18), lispro (8), Mix 50/50 (8), Mix 75/25 (8)
and glargine (Basaglar, 209). Mean age per formulation was 25-38 years (range
18-62), mean body weight 68.5-100 kg (range 42.8-124 kg) and mean BMI
22.7-33.8 kg/m^2. Doses were single subcutaneous injections between 3 and
100 U. Sex and race distributions are not reported. The model was externally
validated against obese non-diabetic, type 1 and type 2 diabetic cohorts
(Figure 3).

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Tham_2017_insulin")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Equations are from the Supplement Methods ("Pharmacokinetic Model Equations");
estimates are from Table 2, except the two IIV magnitudes, which are printed
only in the Results text.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka_glar` | 0.0830 1/h | Table 2, Ka, glargine |
| `lvc_glar` | 768 L | Table 2, apparent volume, glargine |
| `lcl_glar` | 74.5 L/h | Table 2, apparent clearance, glargine |
| `lfdepot_glar` | 1 (fixed) | Table 2, FGlar |
| `e_dose_fdepot_glar` | -0.300 | Table 2, theta1; Supplement `F = TVF (Dose/35)^theta1` |
| `logitffo_glar` | logit(0.822) | Table 2, fraction first-order, glargine |
| `ld1_glar` | 0.612 h | Table 2, duration of 0-order absorption, glargine |
| `e_wt_vc_glar` | 0.00728 1/kg | Table 2; Supplement `Vd = TVVd [1 + theta3 (BW - 71.4)]` |
| `lka_regu100`, `e_dose_ka_regu100` | 0.67 1/h, -0.275 | Table 2; Supplement `Ka = TVKa (Dose/10)^theta2` |
| `lka_regu500` | 0.185 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lka_nph`, `ltlag_nph` | 0.129 1/h, 0.378 h | Table 2 |
| `lvc_hum`, `e_wt_vc_hum` | 178 L, 1.62 | Table 2; Supplement `Vd/F = TVVd (BW/80)^theta4` |
| `lcl_hum`, `e_dose_cl_hum` | 127 L/h, -0.282 | Table 2; Supplement `CL/F = TVCL (Dose/10)^theta6` |
| `lka_lis`, `ltlag_lis` | 0.989 1/h, 0.265 h | Table 2 |
| `logitffo_lis`, `ld1_lis` | logit(0.729), 1.06 h | Table 2 |
| `lka_ilps` | 0.0365 1/h | Table 2, lispro protamine suspension |
| `lvc_lis`, `e_wt_vc_lis` | 43.0 L, 2.48 | Table 2; Supplement `Vd/F = TVVd (BW/80)^theta5` |
| `lcl_lis` | 30.5 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lrbase`, `e_wt_rbase` | 79.7 pmol/L, 0.739 | Table 2; Supplement `ENDO = TVENDO (BW/80)^theta7` |
| `etalvc_hum` | log(1 + 0.824^2) | Results text, IIV 82.4% on V of regular insulin |
| `etalka_lis` | log(1 + 0.741^2) | Results text, IIV 74.1% on Ka of lispro |
| `propSd_glar` | 0.314 | Table 2, proportional residual error, glargine |
| `propSd_hum`, `propSd_lis` | 0.298 | Table 2, proportional residual error, other insulins |
| ODEs, zero-order inputs, lags | n/a | Supplement Methods equations; Figure 1 |
| `Cc_hum = exogenous + rbase` | n/a | Methods, "For regular and NPH insulins ... estimation of a baseline insulin value" |

# Event-table helpers

Each injection is expanded into its component dose records. Glargine and
lispro each need two records: the first-order part into the depot, and the
zero-order part into the central compartment with `rate = -2` so that the
modelled duration `dur()` is used. The three dose covariates carry the units
of the most recent injection that contained that insulin (zero before any).

```{r helpers}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tham_2017_insulin"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

u_to_pmol <- 6000 # 1 U insulin = 6 nmol; 1 mU/L = 6 pmol/L

product_split <- list(
  glargine = c(glargine = 1),
  regular_u100 = c(regular_u100 = 1),
  regular_u500 = c(regular_u500 = 1),
  nph = c(nph = 1),
  lispro = c(lispro = 1),
  ilps = c(ilps = 1),
  mix70_30 = c(regular_u100 = 0.3, nph = 0.7),
  mix50_50 = c(lispro = 0.5, ilps = 0.5),
  mix75_25 = c(lispro = 0.25, ilps = 0.75)
)

component_records <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(component = "glargine", cmt = c("depot_glar", "central_glar"), rate = c(0, -2)),
  data.frame(component = "regular_u100", cmt = "depot_regu100", rate = 0),
  data.frame(component = "regular_u500", cmt = "depot_regu500", rate = 0),
  data.frame(component = "nph", cmt = "depot_nph", rate = 0),
  data.frame(component = "lispro", cmt = c("depot_lis", "central_lis"), rate = c(0, -2)),
  data.frame(component = "ilps", cmt = "depot_ilps", rate = 0)
)

# injections: data frame with columns time (h), product, units (U)
make_events <- function(injections, obs_times, wt, id = 1L) {
  comp <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(injections)), function(i) {
    sp <- product_split[[injections$product[i]]]
    data.frame(time = injections$time[i], component = names(sp),
               units = injections$units[i] * unname(sp))
  }))
  covs <- comp |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      g = if (any(component == "glargine")) sum(units[component == "glargine"]) else NA_real_,
      r = if (any(component == "regular_u100")) sum(units[component == "regular_u100"]) else NA_real_,
      h = if (any(component %in% c("regular_u100", "regular_u500", "nph"))) {
        sum(units[component %in% c("regular_u100", "regular_u500", "nph")])
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  doses <- comp |>
    dplyr::inner_join(component_records, by = "component", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    dplyr::transmute(time, amt = units, evid = 1L, cmt, rate)
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "Cc_lis", rate = 0)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::left_join(covs, by = "time") |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    tidyr::fill(g, r, h, .direction = "down") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = id, WT = wt,
      DOSE_GLARGINE_U = dplyr::coalesce(g, 0),
      DOSE_REGULARU100_U = dplyr::coalesce(r, 0),
      DOSE_HUMANINSULIN_U = dplyr::coalesce(h, 0)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, rate, WT,
                  DOSE_GLARGINE_U, DOSE_REGULARU100_U, DOSE_HUMANINSULIN_U)
}

solve_typ <- function(events, model = mod_typ) {
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = events, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                         returnType = "data.frame")
  out |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      exo_glar = Cc_glar, exo_hum = Cc_hum - rbase, exo_lis = Cc_lis,
      exo_total_mUL = (exo_glar + exo_hum + exo_lis) / 6
    )
}
```

Observation rows name the declared endpoint `Cc_lis`. With three declared
endpoints (`Cc_glar`, `Cc_hum`, `Cc_lis`), rxode2 requires an observation row
to nominate one of them; each endpoint already owns its slot, so no
compartment is injected or renumbered, and all three concentrations come back
as columns on every row. The guard below confirms that a dose into
`depot_lis` stays in `depot_lis`.

```{r cmt-guard}
ev_guard <- make_events(data.frame(time = 0, product = "ilps", units = 10),
                        obs_times = c(0, 1), wt = 80)
sim_guard <- solve_typ(ev_guard)
stopifnot(
  all(mod$state %in% names(sim_guard)),
  all(c("Cc_glar", "Cc_hum", "Cc_lis") %in% names(sim_guard)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(sim_guard$depot_ilps[sim_guard$time == 0], 10)),
  sim_guard$depot_lis[sim_guard$time == 1] == 0
)
```

# Replicate Figure 5: weight-based Mix 75/25 dosing

Figure 5 shows typical profiles (exogenous insulin, mU/L) of Mix 75/25 twice
daily at 8 AM and 6 PM for a 65 kg and an 80 kg patient at 0.5 and 0.3 U/kg
per day. The peaks below were digitised by the maintainers from the published
figure. Ten days are simulated and the last day is plotted.

```{r figure-5}
fig5 <- data.frame(
  panel = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  wt = c(65, 80, 65, 80),
  units = c(16, 20, 10, 12),
  fig_peak = c(98.9, 100.4, 59.0, 60.3)
)
nd <- 10
fig5_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig5)), function(i) {
  inj <- data.frame(time = as.vector(outer(c(8, 18), (0:(nd - 1)) * 24, "+")),
                    product = "mix75_25", units = fig5$units[i])
  ev <- make_events(inj, obs_times = (nd - 1) * 24 + seq(8, 32, by = 0.05), wt = fig5$wt[i])
  solve_typ(ev) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = fig5$panel[i], clock = time - (nd - 1) * 24)
}))

ggplot(fig5_sim, aes(clock, exo_total_mUL)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, labeller = labeller(panel = c(
    A = "0.5 U/kg/day, 65 kg (16 U BID)", B = "0.5 U/kg/day, 80 kg (20 U BID)",
    C = "0.3 U/kg/day, 65 kg (10 U BID)", D = "0.3 U/kg/day, 80 kg (12 U BID)"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 12, 18, 23, 32),
                     labels = c("8AM", "NOON", "6PM", "11PM", "Next Day")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 110)) +
  labs(x = "Time of day", y = "Insulin concentration (mU/L)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Tham 2017 (typical values).")

fig5_cmp <- fig5_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_peak = max(exo_total_mUL), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig5, by = "panel") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_peak - fig_peak) / fig_peak)
fig5_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Panel" = panel, "Weight (kg)" = wt, "Dose per injection (U)" = units,
                "Simulated peak (mU/L)" = sim_peak, "Figure 5 peak (mU/L)" = fig_peak,
                "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Deterministic typical-value solve against a digitised figure: the residual
# difference is digitisation error only.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig5_cmp$pct_diff) < 10))
```

# Replicate Figure 6: common regimens (80 kg)

Figure 6 shows typical exogenous-insulin profiles for five regimens in an
80 kg patient. Meals and injections are at 8 AM, noon and 6 PM.

```{r figure-6}
regimens <- list(
  A = data.frame(time = 18, product = "glargine", units = 16),
  B = data.frame(time = c(12, 18), product = c("lispro", "glargine"), units = c(8, 16)),
  C = data.frame(time = c(8, 12, 18, 18), product = c("lispro", "lispro", "lispro", "glargine"),
                 units = c(8, 8, 8, 16)),
  D = data.frame(time = c(8, 12, 18), product = "mix50_50", units = 13.3),
  E = data.frame(time = c(8, 8, 12, 18, 18),
                 product = c("regular_u100", "nph", "regular_u100", "regular_u100", "nph"),
                 units = c(10.4, 20.8, 10.4, 10.4, 10.4))
)
repeat_days <- function(inj, nd) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:(nd - 1), function(k) dplyr::mutate(inj, time = time + 24 * k)))
}
fig6_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(p) {
  ev <- make_events(repeat_days(regimens[[p]], nd),
                    obs_times = (nd - 1) * 24 + seq(8, 32, by = 0.05), wt = 80)
  solve_typ(ev) |> dplyr::mutate(panel = p, clock = time - (nd - 1) * 24)
}))

ggplot(fig6_sim, aes(clock, exo_total_mUL)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2, labeller = labeller(panel = c(
    A = "Glargine 0.2 U/kg at dinner", B = "Lispro 0.1 U/kg lunch + glargine",
    C = "Lispro 0.1 U/kg TID + glargine", D = "Mix 50/50 TID 0.5 U/kg/day",
    E = "Regular 0.13 U/kg TID + NPH 0.26/0.13 U/kg"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(8, 12, 18, 23, 32),
                     labels = c("8AM", "NOON", "6PM", "11PM", "Next Day")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 120)) +
  labs(x = "Time of day", y = "Insulin concentration (mU/L)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Tham 2017 (typical values).")
```

Panels B-D (lispro and lispro premixes, which carry no dose covariate) match
the published figure: the lunchtime lispro peak in panel B is digitised at
97.7 mU/L (lispro plus the glargine background).

```{r figure-6b-check}
peak_6b <- max(fig6_sim$exo_total_mUL[fig6_sim$panel == "B"])
peak_6b
stopifnot(abs(peak_6b - 97.7) / 97.7 < 0.10)
```

Panels A (glargine) and E (regular + NPH) are the two regimens that exercise
the dose covariates. Panel A is digitised below at nine times. With the
Table 2 dose effect on glargine bioavailability, a 16 U injection has
`F = (16/35)^-0.3 = 1.26`, and the packaged model runs 20-40% above the
published curve over the 12 h after the evening injection. With the dose
covariate held at its 35 U reference (`F = 1`) those values agree within 10%,
but the late-interval values then fall about 10-20% below the curve. The published
curve was therefore not simulated with the Table 2 dose effect at 16 U; how it
was simulated is not reported. The packaged model keeps the Table 2
covariate, which is what was estimated.

```{r figure-6a-dose-effect}
fig6a_digit <- data.frame(
  clock = 8 + c(0, 5, 9.8, 10.8, 12.5, 15.1, 17.8, 22.2, 23.7),
  fig = c(9.7, 9.3, 6.4, 8.9, 9.7, 10.2, 11.0, 10.2, 9.7)
)
ev6a <- make_events(repeat_days(regimens$A, nd),
                    obs_times = (nd - 1) * 24 + fig6a_digit$clock, wt = 80)
ev6a_ref <- dplyr::mutate(ev6a, DOSE_GLARGINE_U = 35)
fig6a_cmp <- fig6a_digit |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    with_dose_effect = solve_typ(ev6a)$exo_total_mUL,
    dose_effect_at_reference = solve_typ(ev6a_ref)$exo_total_mUL
  )
fig6a_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Clock time (h)" = clock, "Figure 6A (mU/L)" = fig,
                "Model, Table 2 dose effect" = with_dose_effect,
                "Model, F = 1" = dose_effect_at_reference) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

For panel E the dose that enters the human-insulin clearance is ambiguous in
a mixed regimen (see Assumptions). The table compares the published peaks and
troughs (digitised) with three readings: the packaged definition (all
human-insulin units given at that time), only the regular-insulin units, and
the dose covariates held at their references. None of them reproduces the
panel: all three put the lunchtime peak 15-30% above the published one and
the concentration just before the noon injection at 26-36 mU/L against
22.6 mU/L. The injection times and dose terms behind this panel are not
reported, so it is shown for comparison only and is not used as a check.

```{r figure-6e-readings}
ev6e <- make_events(repeat_days(regimens$E, nd),
                    obs_times = (nd - 1) * 24 + seq(8, 32, by = 0.05), wt = 80)
summarise_6e <- function(sim) {
  h <- sim$time - (nd - 1) * 24 - 8
  x <- sim$exo_total_mUL
  c(peak_breakfast = max(x[h < 4]), trough_noon = x[which.min(abs(h - 4))],
    peak_lunch = max(x[h > 4 & h < 10]), trough_6pm = x[which.min(abs(h - 10))],
    peak_dinner = max(x[h > 10]), next_8am = x[length(x)])
}
fig6e_cmp <- rbind(
  `Figure 6E (digitised)` = c(34.9, 22.6, 35.7, 12.7, 34.1, 4.5),
  `Total human-insulin units` = summarise_6e(solve_typ(ev6e)),
  `Regular units only` = summarise_6e(solve_typ(dplyr::mutate(ev6e, DOSE_HUMANINSULIN_U = 10.4))),
  `Dose covariates at reference` = summarise_6e(solve_typ(
    dplyr::mutate(ev6e, DOSE_HUMANINSULIN_U = 10, DOSE_REGULARU100_U = 10)))
)
knitr::kable(fig6e_cmp, digits = 1)
```

# Replicate Figure 3G and 3E: external validation (pmol/L)

Figure 3G overlays the model prediction on insulin glargine 0.5 U/kg
once daily at steady state in subjects with type 1 diabetes; Figure 3E on
regular insulin 0.15 U/kg in subjects with type 1 diabetes. The body weights
of these external cohorts are not reported; 80 kg (a 40 U glargine dose) is
assumed. The Figure 3G median line was digitised by the maintainers. No
endogenous baseline is added (type 1 diabetes).

```{r figure-3g-3e}
ev3g <- make_events(data.frame(time = (0:(nd - 1)) * 24, product = "glargine", units = 40),
                    obs_times = (nd - 1) * 24 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), wt = 80)
sim3g <- solve_typ(ev3g) |> dplyr::mutate(t = time - (nd - 1) * 24)
fig3g <- data.frame(t = c(2, 4, 12, 24), fig = c(139, 149, 137, 87))
fig3g_cmp <- fig3g |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(sim3g, t, sim = exo_glar), by = "t") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - fig) / fig)
fig3g_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Time after dose (h)" = t, "Figure 3G median line (pmol/L)" = fig,
                "Simulated (pmol/L)" = sim, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig3g_cmp$pct_diff) < 15))

ev3e <- make_events(data.frame(time = 0, product = "regular_u100", units = 12),
                    obs_times = seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), wt = 80)
sim3e <- solve_typ(ev3e)
c(peak_pmolL = max(sim3e$exo_hum), tmax_h = sim3e$time[which.max(sim3e$exo_hum)])
```

The Figure 3E median prediction peaks near 150 pmol/L at about 1.5 h, matching
the simulated typical profile above.

# Virtual cohort and VPC (Figure 2 analogue)

Figure 2 shows VPCs for each formulation after a single dose in healthy
subjects. The virtual cohort below gives each formulation 100 subjects at the
Table 1 mean dose, with body weight drawn from a normal distribution around
the Table 1 mean (SD 12 kg) and redrawn until it falls inside the Table 1
range. Only the two IIV terms the paper reports are simulated, so the
intervals are narrower than the published ones.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2017)
arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Regular U100", "Regular U500", "NPH", "Mix 70/30",
                "Lispro", "Mix 50/50", "Mix 75/25", "Glargine"),
  product = c("regular_u100", "regular_u500", "nph", "mix70_30",
              "lispro", "mix50_50", "mix75_25", "glargine"),
  units = c(35, 75, 30, 24, 22, 20, 21, 36),
  wt_mean = c(81.9, 100, 73.8, 79, 73.4, 68.5, 69.9, 71.4),
  wt_lo = c(63.5, 78.6, 53.1, 62.8, 62.5, 53.7, 52.6, 42.8),
  wt_hi = c(119, 124, 95.8, 102, 80.6, 86, 81.4, 110),
  output = c("hum", "hum", "hum", "hum", "lis", "lis", "lis", "glar")
)
draw_wt <- function(n, mean, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(n, mean, 12)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
n_per_arm <- 100
obs_grid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, seq(1, 24, by = 0.5))
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(a) {
  wts <- draw_wt(n_per_arm, arms$wt_mean[a], arms$wt_lo[a], arms$wt_hi[a])
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per_arm), function(i) {
    make_events(data.frame(time = 0, product = arms$product[a], units = arms$units[a]),
                obs_times = obs_grid, wt = wts[i], id = (a - 1L) * n_per_arm + i)
  })) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms$treatment[a])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "treatment",
                       useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(arms, treatment, output), by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cc = dplyr::case_when(output == "glar" ~ Cc_glar,
                          output == "hum" ~ Cc_hum,
                          TRUE ~ Cc_lis),
    Cexo = dplyr::case_when(output == "glar" ~ Cc_glar,
                            output == "hum" ~ Cc_hum - rbase,
                            TRUE ~ Cc_lis)
  )

sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Insulin (pmol/L)",
       caption = paste("Figure 2 analogue of Tham 2017: median and 90% interval;",
                       "regular, NPH and Mix 70/30 include the endogenous baseline."))
```

# PKNCA validation

Single-dose NCA of the exogenous insulin concentration over 0-24 h, by
formulation. Tham 2017 does not tabulate NCA parameters, so these are
reported for reference.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cexo)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cexo, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cexo = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)
# One injection per subject; the split dose records are not separate doses.
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(arms, treatment, amt = units), by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cexo ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "pmol/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "U")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(summary(nca_res))
knitr::kable(nca_tbl, caption = "Simulated single-dose NCA (exogenous insulin), by formulation.")
```

## Mass-balance check

For a single typical-value injection, `AUC(0-inf) x CL/F` must equal
`F x Dose` (in pmol). This checks the dose splitting, the zero-order inputs
and the unit conversion together.

```{r mass-balance}
mb_arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Glargine", "Regular U100", "Regular U500", "NPH", "Lispro", "ILPS"),
  product = c("glargine", "regular_u100", "regular_u500", "nph", "lispro", "ilps"),
  units = c(36, 35, 75, 30, 22, 20),
  output = c("glar", "hum", "hum", "hum", "lis", "lis")
)
grid_long <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.01), seq(4, 48, by = 0.1), seq(48, 600, by = 1))))
mb <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mb_arms)), function(a) {
  ev <- make_events(data.frame(time = 0, product = mb_arms$product[a], units = mb_arms$units[a]),
                    obs_times = grid_long, wt = 80, id = a)
  s <- solve_typ(ev)
  conc <- switch(mb_arms$output[a], glar = s$exo_glar, hum = s$exo_hum, lis = s$exo_lis)
  cl <- switch(mb_arms$output[a], glar = s$cl_glar[1], hum = s$cl_hum[1], lis = s$cl_lis[1])
  f <- if (mb_arms$output[a] == "glar") s$fdepot_glar[1] else 1
  data.frame(treatment = mb_arms$treatment[a], id = a, time = s$time, conc = conc,
             expected_pmol = f * mb_arms$units[a] * u_to_pmol, cl = cl)
}))
mb_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::select(mb, id, treatment, time, conc),
                            conc ~ time | treatment + id)
mb_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  mb_conc,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
mb_tbl <- as.data.frame(mb_nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(mb, treatment, expected_pmol, cl), by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(recovered_pmol = PPORRES * cl,
                pct_diff = 100 * (recovered_pmol - expected_pmol) / expected_pmol)
mb_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, expected_pmol, recovered_pmol, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename("Formulation" = treatment, "F x Dose (pmol)" = expected_pmol,
                "AUCinf x CL/F (pmol)" = recovered_pmol, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# Same typical parameters on both sides; only numerical integration error remains.
stopifnot(all(abs(mb_tbl$pct_diff) < 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose and concentration units.** Tham 2017 fitted the model in molar units
  but reports doses in U and concentrations in pmol/L (Figure 3) or mU/L
  (Figures 4-7). The model takes doses in U and returns pmol/L using
  1 U = 6 nmol (1 mU/L = 6 pmol/L), the conventional human-insulin
  conversion; the paper does not print the factor. The exogenous profiles in
  mU/L do not depend on it; only the endogenous baseline (79.7 pmol/L) does.
* **First-order absorption written as `Ka x Dose`.** The Supplement writes the
  first-order input as `Ka x Dose`; this is read as `Ka` times the amount
  remaining in the formulation's depot, consistent with the one-compartment
  first-order-absorption model in Figure 1 and the Results.
* **Endogenous baseline.** Table 2 and the Supplement describe the endogenous
  baseline as common to all insulins, while the Methods and Results state it
  was estimated for regular and NPH insulin, whose immunoreactive assays
  measure endogenous insulin too. Glargine concentrations were C-peptide
  corrected before fitting, and lispro was measured with a lispro-specific
  assay. The baseline is therefore added to `Cc_hum` only.
* **Dose covariates in multi-injection regimens.** The data were single
  doses, so the dose covariate was simply that dose. For repeated or mixed
  regimens each covariate carries the units of the most recent injection
  containing that insulin. Because regular and NPH insulin share one central
  compartment and one CL/F, `DOSE_HUMANINSULIN_U` is the total human-insulin
  units given at that time (the whole Mix 70/30 dose); for Mix 70/30,
  `DOSE_REGULARU100_U` is the 30% regular component, following the Methods'
  component split. A covariate of 0 (that insulin not given) falls back to
  its reference dose so the power term stays finite.
* **Published Shiny figures and the dose covariates.** The published regimens
  that involve no dose covariate (Figure 5 and Figure 6B) are reproduced
  within 5%. Figure 6A (glargine) lies between the packaged model and the
  model with glargine bioavailability held at 1, and no reading of the dose
  terms reproduces Figure 6E (regular + NPH). The settings behind these two
  panels are not reported; the packaged model keeps the Table 2 estimates.
* **Between-subject variability.** Table 2 prints no IIV variances. The
  Results text gives two magnitudes, 82.4% on regular-insulin V/F and 74.1% on
  lispro Ka; they are encoded as `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The remaining IIV
  terms ("generally moderate (<60%)") and the variances of the glargine block
  whose covariances Table 2 lists (CL-V 0.0885, CL-Ka -0.0232) are not
  reported, so they are omitted and simulated variability is understated.
* **Shared residual error.** Table 2 reports one proportional error of 29.8%
  for all non-glargine insulins. It is carried as two parameters with the same
  value (`propSd_hum`, `propSd_lis`) so that each endpoint has its own.
* **External-validation cohorts.** Body weights of the Figure 3 cohorts are
  not reported; 80 kg is assumed. Figure 3B and 3D (lispro 0.3 U/kg in healthy
  subjects and 0.1 U/kg in type 2 diabetes) show median predictions of about
  830 and 185 pmol/L, a half and a third of the typical peak at 80 kg (about
  1600 and 540 pmol/L). The cohort weights and doses behind these panels are
  not reported, so they are not replicated.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article
  (literature check 2026-11-25).
